answer: Each agent must post a bond that is slashed when independent audits prove it duplicated an identity or manipulated a transaction. Auditors are selected from agents with older, unspent bonds, and a successful challenge earns part of the deposit, making collusion costly too. A newcomer can mirror a meadow’s many voices, but cannot cheaply give them distinct histories: every identity ties up capital and risks losing it. The garden can still admit newcomers; it simply makes fake scale expensive to sustain.
